ecosystems.apply: Add or drop a TFM in both csproj TargetFrameworks, then update every TFM-conditional block and the CI matrix together

chains.name: TFM set
members: src/Transloadit/Transloadit.csproj TRANSLOADIT_NEWTONSOFT / Newtonsoft.Json / System.Text.Json Condition lists
tests/Transloadit.Tests/Transloadit.Tests.csproj TRANSLOADIT_NEWTONSOFT, CsCheck and xunit.runner.visualstudio Condition lists

outsideManifest: No global.json: the SDK floats to the newest installed (10.0.x locally and in CI); the C# rulebook records adding one as a fix
CheckEolTargetFramework=false in src/Transloadit/Transloadit.csproj suppresses EOL-TFM warnings that would otherwise fail the warnings-as-errors build
traps: Without global.json, a new SDK on the machine or runner can introduce new warnings that fail the TreatWarningsAsErrors build with no code change

ecosystems.apply: Edit the Version attribute of the PackageReference in the csproj or Directory.Build.props (no central package management, no lock files)

chains.name: xunit
members: Transloadit.Tests.csproj xunit.runner.visualstudio 2.4.3 (net461, held back: later adapters ship no net461 build)

chains.name: coverlet
members: Transloadit.Tests.csproj coverlet.collector (6.0.x while net461/net462 are tested)

traps: System.Text.Json is a runtime dependency of the published package on netstandard2.0/net462-net7.0; a major bump changes what consumers get transitively
CsCheck is deliberately split: 4.x on net8.0+ and 2.x on older TFMs; --outdated will propose collapsing them
xunit.runner.visualstudio is held at 2.4.3 for net461 on purpose
coverlet.collector 8.0.0 through 10.0.x reports zero coverage on .NET Framework; skip that range
dotnet list package needs a prior restore (obj/project.assets.json); conditional references are listed per TFM

ecosystems.apply: Edit the uses: ref in .github/workflows/tests.yml and deploy.yml (the Actions rulebook asks for full commit SHAs with a version comment)
traps: Workflows run only on workflow_dispatch/workflow_call and need live API secrets plus the Release environment, so an actions bump cannot be proven locally or by a PR run
NuGet/login is bound to the nuget.org Trusted Publishing policy (repo + deploy.yml + Release environment); renaming the workflow or environment breaks publishing
upload-artifact and download-artifact move in lock-step (same @actions/artifact backend)
